sentence: This project tests whether probiotic and blueberry treatments reduce changes in immune cells that come with aging in people with HIV who use alcohol.
This project tries to find out which immune cells in human dorsal root ganglia release interferon gamma and how it may cause neuropathic pain.
This project analyzes imaging and patient data collected in cancer studies and processes advanced images for research groups.
This project builds an imaging technology to understand how genome structure affects gene expression in cells of the developing embryo.
This project provides analysis platforms for metabolomics, epigenomics, transcriptomics and proteomics to support several research projects.
This project studies how stem cells in the outermost layer of blood vessels cause calcium build-up in blood vessels.
This project builds a collection of blood and imaging data from patients to test biomarkers for early detection of hepatocellular carcinoma.
This project builds a way to culture human breast cancer cells in a mammary duct model to study how the cells invade the duct.
This project builds programs that help researchers carry out clinical and translational research.
This project studies how Toll-like receptors turn on genes that drive systemic lupus erythematosus, using mouse models.
This project studies the basic mechanisms that control normal and malignant hematopoiesis and works on ways to treat hematopoietic malignancies.
This project combines imaging technologies to find biomarkers that show at diagnosis which men with prostate cancer will develop lethal disease.
This project develops an oncolytic adenovirus that targets colorectal cancer and allows imaging and therapy with radioactive iodine.
This project develops methods that map cell types and how they are arranged in the human brain, using single-cell transcriptomics and epigenomics.
This project studies how long-range regulatory elements control the tumor necrosis factor gene in a cell-type specific manner.
This project studies how proximal tubule injury leads to DNA damage and pro-inflammatory cytokines in chronic kidney disease, using human samples and animal models.
This project studies how microbes survive and persist indoors in flood-contaminated materials like drywall, insulation, wood and concrete.
This project maintains a collection of virus strains and related reagents for research on emerging viruses and arthropod-borne viruses.
This project develops mRNA lipid nanoparticles that steer the immune response and tests them in mouse cancer models.
This project provides tools to study how brain cells and circuits work in intellectual and developmental disabilities, using electrophysiological approaches and cerebral organoids.
